philosophy.audience: Native English speaker, Year 5–6 Australian Scholarship prep
philosophy.chinese_field: Parent reference only — never shown in student lessons

words.definition: Present in a large amount; more than enough.
words.example_sentence: The library offered abundant evidence for both sides of the debate.

words.definition: Correct in every important detail.
words.example_sentence: An accurate account of the experiment must include the unexpected result.
words.writing_value: Essential for science and comprehension answers.

words.definition: To change behaviour or method so that it fits a new situation.
words.example_sentence: Oliver had to adapt his study routine when cricket training moved to Thursday nights.
words.writing_value: Useful for character growth and problem-solving.

words.definition: To give someone a thoughtful recommendation about what to do.
words.example_sentence: The teacher did not order him to rewrite the paragraph; she advised him to tighten the opening.
words.writing_value: Separates the verb from the noun "advice".

words.definition: Belonging to a time long ago; very old.
words.example_sentence: The museum case held an ancient compass used on early coastal voyages.

words.definition: Feeling worried or uneasy about what may happen.
words.example_sentence: He felt anxious before the scholarship paper, but he still read the first question twice.

words.definition: Easy to see or understand; seeming to be true.
words.example_sentence: It became apparent that the missing page had been torn out, not lost.

words.definition: To come nearer, or a way of dealing with a task.
words.example_sentence: A careful approach to the comprehension passage saved him from a trap in question three.
words.writing_value: Works as noun or verb in academic writing.

words.definition: Uncomfortable, clumsy, or difficult to handle.
words.example_sentence: An awkward silence followed when nobody wanted to admit the mistake.
words.writing_value: Good for social tension in stories.

words.definition: Lasting only a short time; using few words.
words.example_sentence: The examiner asked for a brief summary, not a retelling of every sentence.
words.writing_value: Signals control of length in writing.

words.definition: Having the skill or quality needed to do something well.
words.example_sentence: She was capable of solving the puzzle, but she refused to rush.

words.definition: Careful to avoid danger, error, or unnecessary risk.
words.example_sentence: A cautious reader checks whether the narrator can be trusted.

words.definition: To come to an end or to stop doing something.
words.example_sentence: The rain did not cease until the creek had risen over the crossing.

words.definition: Quick to understand, invent, or notice.
words.example_sentence: The clever solution used the leftover string instead of asking for new equipment.
words.writing_value: Can praise or warn, depending on tone.

words.definition: To begin, especially in a formal or planned way.
words.example_sentence: The examination will commence at nine, whether every pencil is sharp or not.
words.writing_value: Formal register for instructions and reports.

words.definition: To examine two or more things to see how they are alike or different.
words.example_sentence: Compare the two openings and decide which one earns the reader’s trust faster.

words.definition: Whole, or finished with nothing important missing.
words.example_sentence: A complete answer names the reason, not only the event.

words.definition: To think about something carefully before judging it.
words.example_sentence: Consider the evidence before you decide that the narrator is cruel.

words.definition: The quality of facing fear, pain, or difficulty with resolve.
words.example_sentence: It took courage to admit that the winning idea had not been his.
words.writing_value: Stronger than "being brave" in character essays.

words.definition: Eager to know or learn; unusual enough to attract attention.

words.definition: To refuse politely, or to become smaller or weaker.
words.example_sentence: He chose to decline the easier class even though the harder one looked intimidating.

words.definition: Clear and unlikely to change; certain.

words.definition: Easily damaged, or requiring sensitive handling.
words.example_sentence: It was a delicate situation: telling the truth would hurt someone who had tried to help.
words.writing_value: Good for social and physical description.

words.definition: To show clearly by evidence, action, or example.

words.definition: Packed closely together; difficult to see through or to understand.

words.definition: To need someone or something for support or success.

words.definition: To say what someone or something is like, using precise detail.

words.definition: To have earned a particular treatment or result.

words.definition: To decide firmly, or to find out the facts.

words.definition: A tool or machine, or a method used to achieve an effect.

words.definition: Working carefully and steadily, with proper attention.
words.example_sentence: Diligent checking caught the reversed digits before the answer was submitted.

words.definition: Clearly different or easy to recognise separately.

words.definition: Wanting to do or have something very much.

words.definition: Extremely large in size, amount, or importance.

words.definition: Absolutely necessary; of the greatest importance.

words.definition: Easy to see or understand; obvious from the facts.

words.definition: Well known because it has been seen or experienced before.

words.definition: Happening often.

words.definition: Willing to give more than is necessary or expected.

words.definition: Happening slowly, in small stages.

words.definition: Telling the truth and refusing to cheat or pretend.

words.definition: To recognise and name someone or something correctly.
words.example_sentence: First identify the question type; then choose a method.

words.definition: To form a picture or idea in the mind.
words.example_sentence: Imagine the hall at 8:55: bags at the wall, nobody talking above a whisper.

words.definition: To make or become better.

words.definition: To make something part of a larger whole.

words.definition: Able to think or act without needing to be controlled.

words.definition: To show or point to a fact, often without stating it directly.

words.definition: To have a plan or purpose in mind.

words.definition: An act of travelling from one place to another, or a long process of change.

words.definition: Probable; reasonably expected to happen or be true.

words.definition: Extremely impressive or beautiful.

words.definition: Needed in order for something to happen or be complete.

words.definition: Easy for anyone to see or understand.

words.definition: Normal; not special, extreme, or unusual.

words.definition: Used to single out one thing from others; specific.

words.definition: Able to wait or keep trying without becoming angry.
words.example_sentence: A patient rereading found the pronoun that the first reading had skipped.

words.definition: Strange, unusual, or belonging to one particular person or place.

words.definition: Enjoyable, friendly, or giving a sense of ease.

words.definition: To stop something from happening or someone from doing something.

words.definition: The reason something is done or created.

words.definition: Happening very quickly.
words.example_sentence: Rapid guessing is how easy marks disappear.

words.definition: Having happened or been made not long ago.

words.definition: To need something as necessary.
words.example_sentence: The question does not require a story; it requires a reason.

words.definition: Almost the same, but not identical.

words.definition: Happening quickly and without warning.

words.definition: To put forward an idea, or to hint that something is true.
words.example_sentence: The final image suggests regret without naming it.

words.definition: Complete and careful, with nothing important missed.

words.definition: Not common or ordinary; surprising because it is different.

words.definition: Worth a great deal of money, time, or attention.

words.definition: Several different kinds.

words.definition: Showing fondness or gentle care.

words.definition: Ready to attack, argue, or push forward forcefully.

words.definition: Determined to achieve success or a demanding goal.

words.definition: Anxious that something unpleasant may happen.

words.definition: Behaving as if superior to others and unwilling to listen.

words.definition: Feeling guilt or embarrassment about something done or left undone.

words.definition: Angry and hurt because of unfairness or disappointment.

words.definition: Too proud of one’s own abilities or appearance.

words.definition: Feeling awkward or ashamed in front of others.

words.definition: Wanting what another person has.

words.definition: Loyal and reliable; true to a person, duty, or idea.

words.definition: Intense, forceful, or showing strong feeling.

words.definition: To stop blaming someone for an offence.

words.definition: Extremely angry.

words.definition: Feeling thankful for help or a kindness.

words.definition: Wanting more than is fair or needed.

words.definition: Slow to act or speak because of uncertainty.

words.definition: Not proud or boastful; modest about ability or status.

words.definition: Unwilling to wait; easily irritated by delay.

words.definition: Acting suddenly, without enough thought.

words.definition: Not interested or concerned; neither for nor against.

words.definition: Not confident; uncertain about oneself or a situation.

words.definition: Easily annoyed, especially when tired or tense.
words.example_sentence: He grew irritable when the same instruction was repeated, which was a warning to himself.

words.definition: Afraid of losing someone’s attention, or resentful of a rival.

words.definition: Firm in support of a person, group, or idea.

words.definition: Intending to hurt or upset someone.

words.writing_value: Strong moral word; do not overuse.

words.definition: A deep, quiet sadness, often without a single simple cause.
words.example_sentence: A trace of melancholy sat under the joke, and the best readers noticed it.

words.definition: Playfully causing trouble, usually without serious harm.

words.definition: Not talking about one’s abilities; moderate rather than showy.

words.definition: Willing to follow rules or instructions.

words.definition: Expecting good outcomes; hopeful about the future.

words.definition: Showing strong feeling or commitment.

words.definition: Expecting the worst; seeing difficulties more clearly than hope.

words.definition: Pleased with an achievement, or having too high an opinion of oneself.

words.definition: Resisting control, custom, or authority.
words.example_sentence: A rebellious streak can be intelligence wearing a louder jacket.

words.definition: Not willing or eager to do something.

words.definition: Feeling bitter because of unfair treatment.
words.example_sentence: He felt resentful that effort had been praised less than natural speed.

words.definition: Showing regard for people, rules, or serious situations.

words.definition: Caring chiefly for oneself and not for others.

words.definition: Genuine; not pretended or performed.

words.definition: Serious, formal, and without playfulness.

words.definition: Unwilling to change one’s mind or course.

words.definition: Understanding and sharing another person’s feelings.

words.definition: Easily frightened; lacking confidence in company or action.

words.definition: Too concerned with appearance or praise; also, unsuccessful.

words.definition: Wanting to harm someone in return for a wrong.

words.definition: Open to being hurt, physically or emotionally.
words.example_sentence: He felt vulnerable standing at the front, which is why the first sentence had to be ready.

words.definition: Very tired, often after long effort or worry.
words.example_sentence: The weary group still finished the last kilometre without complaint.

words.definition: Clever and amusing with words.
words.example_sentence: A witty remark can rescue a tense room or wound the wrong person.

words.definition: Cold, empty, and without comfort or hope.

words.definition: In a state of complete disorder and confusion.
words.example_sentence: The chaotic morning still produced a quiet, well-ruled exam paper.

words.definition: Extremely large; astonishing in scale.
words.example_sentence: Losing five marks to sloppy reading felt like a colossal mistake.

words.definition: Hidden so that it cannot easily be seen or known.

words.definition: Very easy to notice; attracting attention.

words.definition: Skilful at achieving goals by clever, sometimes dishonest, means.

words.definition: Extremely bright or impressive.

words.definition: Done on purpose, or slow and careful in thought.

words.definition: Empty, lonely, and without life or comfort.

words.definition: Careful not to attract attention or cause embarrassment.

words.definition: Strange in a way that makes one uneasy.

words.definition: Detailed and complicated; to add more detail.
words.example_sentence: Do not elaborate on a point you cannot support.

words.definition: Fluent, graceful, and persuasive in speech or writing.
words.example_sentence: The most eloquent sentence in the piece was also the shortest.

words.definition: Expressed with force and clarity; leaving no doubt.
words.example_sentence: Her emphatic pause before "however" told the class to listen.

words.definition: To surround and cover completely.

words.definition: A person, thing, or situation that is mysterious and hard to understand.

words.definition: To hold someone’s complete attention; to fascinate.

words.definition: To escape or avoid, especially by cleverness or delay.

words.definition: Unusually good, or unusual in a way that stands apart.

words.definition: Stated clearly and in detail, leaving no room for confusion.

words.definition: Extremely beautiful, delicate, or finely made.

words.definition: Covering a large area or a great amount.

words.definition: Weak in body, argument, or effect.

words.definition: Lasting for a very short time.

words.definition: Inspiring respect or fear because of size, difficulty, or strength.

words.definition: Easily broken, damaged, or upset.

words.definition: Unpleasant, stern, or without hope.

words.definition: Unpleasantly severe, rough, or cruel.

words.definition: Unfriendly, opposing, or difficult to survive in.

words.definition: Extremely large or great.
words.example_sentence: Immense pressure does not excuse a dishonest shortcut.

words.definition: Having many small parts arranged in a complicated way.

words.definition: Far from others; separated from help, company, or connection.

words.definition: Rich, generous, or more expensive than necessary.

words.definition: Having impressive beauty, dignity, or power.

words.definition: Not well known, or not easy to understand.

words.definition: Suggesting that something bad is coming.

words.definition: Extremely large in area, amount, or range.

words.definition: Producing strong, clear images or feelings.

words.definition: To state the exact meaning of a word or idea.
words.example_sentence: Define the problem before you invent a solution.

words.definition: To obtain something from a source, or to reach a conclusion.
words.example_sentence: What conclusion can you derive from the last two sentences together?

words.definition: An essential part of something.
words.example_sentence: Suspense is an element of the passage, not the whole point.

words.definition: To set up, or to show that something is true.
words.example_sentence: The first paragraph must establish the conflict, not wander.

words.definition: To judge an amount or value roughly, using available information.
words.example_sentence: Estimate the word count; then cut the sentence that repeats itself.

words.definition: To judge how good, useful, or successful something is.
words.example_sentence: Evaluate the argument, not the person making it.

words.definition: Facts or details that support a belief or conclusion.
words.example_sentence: Opinion without evidence is just volume.

words.definition: One of the things that influences a result.
words.example_sentence: Time of day was a factor in how carefully they read.

words.definition: The purpose or job that something has.
words.example_sentence: What is the function of the short final paragraph?

words.definition: A possible explanation that can be tested.
words.example_sentence: A hypothesis is a disciplined guess, not a wild one.

words.definition: To make an idea clearer with an example or image.
words.example_sentence: One concrete scene can illustrate a claim better than three adjectives.

words.definition: Something suggested without being said directly, or a likely result.
words.example_sentence: The implication of the last line is that nobody has told the truth yet.

words.definition: To reach a conclusion from evidence rather than from a direct statement.
words.example_sentence: What can the reader infer about the missing letter?

words.definition: To explain the meaning of words, data, or events.
words.example_sentence: Two readers can interpret the same silence in opposite ways; both need evidence.

words.definition: To examine the facts of a situation carefully.
words.example_sentence: Investigate the unusual word before you skip it.

words.definition: To give reasons that show why something is right or reasonable.
words.example_sentence: Justify your answer with a phrase from the passage, not with "I just think".

words.definition: A planned way of doing something.
words.example_sentence: A methodical check of units prevents a certain kind of disaster.

words.definition: To happen, or to come into the mind.
words.example_sentence: It occurred to him that the easiest option was also the least honest.

words.definition: The result of a process, test, or decision.
words.example_sentence: The outcome of rushing is usually a neat page with the wrong answer.

words.definition: A particular way of seeing or thinking about something.
words.example_sentence: A shift in perspective at the end of a story is often the whole point.

words.definition: A fact or event that can be observed, especially one that is unusual.
words.example_sentence: A mirage is a phenomenon, not a hallucination you can argue with.

words.definition: To say what is likely to happen, based on evidence.
words.example_sentence: Predict the ending only after you have noticed the pattern.

words.definition: Coming before in time or order.
words.example_sentence: The previous paragraph already answered the question you are still worrying about.

words.definition: First in importance, or first in a sequence.
words.example_sentence: The primary reason for the delay was not weather; it was a locked gate.

words.definition: A basic rule, belief, or truth that guides action.
words.example_sentence: In principle the rule was fair; in practice it punished the late bus.

words.definition: An agreed series of actions for doing a task.
words.example_sentence: The procedure was posted on the wall, which did not stop people from inventing a faster one.

words.definition: A series of actions that produce a result.
words.example_sentence: Revision is a process, not a single heroic night.

words.definition: Closely connected to the matter being considered.
words.example_sentence: A beautiful sentence is still a waste if it is not relevant.

words.definition: Careful study to discover or check facts.
words.example_sentence: Research a word’s family and you will remember it longer than a translation will allow.

words.definition: Something that can be used to help achieve a goal.
words.example_sentence: Time is a resource; spending it on panic is a poor investment.

words.definition: To reply or react, in words or action.
words.example_sentence: Respond to the question that was asked, not the one you wished had been asked.

words.definition: The function or part played by a person or thing.
words.example_sentence: What role does the weather play in the character’s decision?

words.definition: The order in which things follow one another.
words.example_sentence: A muddled sequence of events is often why a narrative loses marks.

words.definition: Important enough to be worth noticing or discussing.
words.example_sentence: A significant detail is usually repeated, stressed, or strangely ordinary.

words.definition: The place, person, or text from which something comes.
words.example_sentence: Name the source of a fact, or do not treat it as a fact.

words.definition: Clearly identified; particular rather than general.
words.example_sentence: Be specific: "the cracked compass" is better than "the thing".

words.definition: A planned method for achieving a goal.
words.example_sentence: A strategy for hard passages is to mark names, times, and shifts in tone.

words.definition: The way parts are arranged to form a whole.
words.example_sentence: The structure of the passage — claim, example, twist — is itself a clue.

words.definition: Coming after something else in time.
words.example_sentence: Subsequent events make the first promise look either brave or foolish.

words.definition: As much as is needed; enough.
words.example_sentence: Two precise quotes are sufficient; five vague ones are not.

words.definition: A system of ideas that explains something, or an unproven idea.
words.example_sentence: In theory the shortcut saved time; in practice it cost the mark.

words.definition: Based on truth or sound reasoning; legally or logically acceptable.
words.example_sentence: A valid point can still be incomplete.

words.definition: To differ, or to change within a range.
words.example_sentence: Answers will vary, but the best ones still quote the text.

words.definition: To succeed in reaching a goal, especially after effort.
words.example_sentence: You do not achieve a scholarship by collecting long words; you achieve it by using the right ones.

words.definition: To gain or come to have something, especially knowledge or a skill.
words.example_sentence: Students acquire vocabulary faster when they meet it in a passage, not only in a list.

words.definition: Suitable for a particular purpose, person, or situation.
words.example_sentence: An appropriate tone for a scholarship letter is respectful, not theatrical.

words.definition: Having more than one possible meaning; unclear.
words.example_sentence: An ambiguous ending is not a failed ending if the uncertainty is the point.

words.definition: Having mixed or opposing feelings about something.
words.example_sentence: He felt ambivalent about winning if it meant a friend went home disappointed.

words.definition: Comparable in a way that helps explanation.
words.example_sentence: The trapped animal is analogous to the character’s fear, not a random extra scene.

words.definition: Based on personal choice or chance rather than reason or a system.
words.example_sentence: An arbitrary rule invites rebellion; a explained rule invites debate.

words.definition: Able to express ideas clearly; to express an idea clearly.
words.example_sentence: He could not yet articulate why the ending felt unfair, but he could point to the broken promise.

words.definition: To find something out for certain.
words.example_sentence: Ascertain what the question actually asks before you start the heroic paragraph.

words.definition: To state a claim firmly.
words.example_sentence: Anyone can assert a claim; the marks go to the student who supports it.

words.definition: To reach or achieve something after effort.
words.example_sentence: Precision is a standard you attain by cutting, not by decorating.

words.definition: To regard something as caused by; a quality belonging to a person.
words.example_sentence: Do not attribute the victory to luck until you have listed the hours of practice.

words.definition: Genuine; not copied, fake, or pretended.
words.example_sentence: An authentic voice in a story sounds like a person, not a brochure.

words.definition: The right or ability to make one’s own decisions.
words.example_sentence: Year 6 students want more autonomy, which is why trust matters more than extra rules.

words.definition: Kind and wanting to do good.
words.example_sentence: A benevolent teacher can still mark strictly.

words.definition: Honest and direct, even when the truth is uncomfortable.
words.example_sentence: Her candid assessment of the draft stung, and then it helped.

words.definition: Including all or nearly all important parts.
words.example_sentence: A comprehensive review is not the same as an endless one.

words.definition: Belonging to the present time, or existing at the same time.
words.example_sentence: A contemporary issue can still be discussed with old-fashioned care.

words.definition: Causing public disagreement or strong opposing views.
words.example_sentence: A controversial decision needs clearer reasons, not a louder announcement.

words.definition: Following accepted custom or the usual way of doing things.
words.example_sentence: Conventional wisdom said the quiet student would not debate; conventional wisdom was wrong.

words.definition: Increasing by successive additions.
words.example_sentence: Vocabulary has a cumulative effect: ten precise words change a whole page.

words.definition: Causing harm or damage.
words.example_sentence: Sleep loss is more detrimental to a scholarship paper than an extra hour of cramming.

words.definition: A difference between two things that should match.
words.example_sentence: The discrepancy between the two witness statements is the beginning of the mystery.

words.definition: Based on observation or experiment rather than theory alone.
words.example_sentence: An empirical test of the creek water is worth more than a confident rumour.

words.definition: Difficult to interpret; mysterious.
words.example_sentence: The enigmatic smile in the photograph became the whole essay question.

words.definition: Lasting for a very short time.
words.example_sentence: The applause was ephemeral; the improved habit was not.

words.definition: Equal in value, meaning, or effect.
words.example_sentence: A precise short answer can be equivalent to a long, wandering one — and better.

words.definition: To make an action or process easier.
words.example_sentence: Clear instructions facilitate speed; unclear ones waste it.

words.definition: Forming a necessary base; of central importance.
words.example_sentence: A fundamental error in reading the question cannot be repaired by beautiful handwriting.

words.definition: Suggested or understood without being directly stated.
words.example_sentence: The criticism is implicit in the last adjective.

words.definition: Originating in a particular place; native to a region.
words.example_sentence: The garden used indigenous plants that could survive a dry January.
words.writing_value: Australian context — capital I for people.

words.definition: Certain to happen and unable to be avoided.
words.example_sentence: If nobody checks the quote, a misread word is inevitable.

words.definition: Existing as a natural or permanent part of something.
words.example_sentence: There is an inherent risk in trusting a charming narrator.

words.definition: Introducing new ideas or methods.
words.example_sentence: An innovative approach is welcome if it still answers the question.

words.definition: Necessary to make a whole complete.
words.example_sentence: Rereading is integral to comprehension, not a sign of weakness.

words.definition: Allowed by rules or reason; genuine.
words.example_sentence: Fear of a hard paper is a legitimate feeling; skipping the reading is not a legitimate strategy.

words.definition: Extremely careful about small details.
words.example_sentence: Meticulous notes are useless if they are never reread.

words.definition: So small that it can be ignored.
words.example_sentence: The difference between the two options was not negligible; one word reversed the meaning.

words.definition: Showy in a way meant to impress others.
words.example_sentence: Ostentatious vocabulary is not the same as precise vocabulary.

words.definition: A statement or situation that seems contradictory but may be true.
words.example_sentence: The paradox of the exam is that slowing down often saves time.

words.definition: Evoking a sharp sense of sadness or regret.
words.example_sentence: The most poignant detail was the unused second lunch, packed by someone who hoped.

words.definition: Dealing with things in a practical, realistic way.
words.example_sentence: A pragmatic plan for the paper was to finish the sure marks before the beautiful ones.

words.definition: More important, powerful, or noticeable than others.
words.example_sentence: The predominant tone of the letter is disappointment, not anger.

words.definition: Coming before the main event or discussion; introductory.
words.example_sentence: A preliminary reading finds the topic; a second reading finds the attitude.

words.definition: Widespread or commonly occurring at a particular time.
words.example_sentence: A prevalent belief in the class was that speed equalled intelligence.

words.definition: Able to recover quickly from difficulty.
words.example_sentence: A resilient student treats a poor practice paper as information, not as a verdict.

words.definition: Large in amount, importance, or worth.
words.example_sentence: You need substantial evidence, not a single convenient line.

words.definition: More than is needed; unnecessary.
words.example_sentence: Cut the superfluous adjective and the sentence usually improves.

words.definition: Likely to be influenced or harmed by something.
words.example_sentence: Tired readers are susceptible to the first attractive option.

words.definition: Holding firmly to a purpose, idea, or position.
words.example_sentence: Tenacious rereading of one hard paragraph is often worth more than skimming three easy ones.

words.definition: Not certain or fixed; done cautiously.
words.example_sentence: A tentative conclusion is honest when the evidence is thin.

words.definition: Seeming to be everywhere at once.
words.example_sentence: The ubiquitous advice to "just be yourself" is unhelpful without a practised skill.

words.definition: Never known or done before.
words.example_sentence: An unprecedented heatwave does not excuse an unprecedented lack of planning.

words.definition: Able to be used, or to perform, in many different ways.
words.example_sentence: A versatile word like "charge" changes meaning with context; that is why exams love it.

words.definition: Capable of working successfully.
words.example_sentence: A viable study plan includes sleep, not only ambition.

words.definition: To accept or admit that something is true or exists.
words.example_sentence: Acknowledge the counter-argument if you want your own to look adult.

words.definition: To set something aside for a particular purpose.
words.example_sentence: Allocate seven minutes to the hardest passage, then move on.

words.definition: To expect something and, often, prepare for it.
words.example_sentence: Anticipate a trap in any question that looks too kind.

words.definition: To collect information from different places and put it together.
words.example_sentence: Compile your error list weekly or you will sit the same trap again.

words.definition: To act in accordance with a rule or request.
words.example_sentence: Students must comply with the silent-paper rule even when the clock feels cruel.

words.definition: To be the parts or the official making of something.
words.example_sentence: Two similar mistakes can constitute a pattern.

words.definition: To reach a logical conclusion from known facts.
words.example_sentence: From the muddy shoes and the early bell, they could deduce he had run.

words.definition: To recognise or show the difference between things.
words.example_sentence: Differentiate "imply" from "infer" and you will stop losing easy marks.
